name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q01 - Cellular level of organisation in sponges

questiontext.text: Which of the following animals exhibits a cellular level of organisation where cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates with some division of labour?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In the animal kingdom, multicellular organisms exhibit different patterns of cell organisation, ranging from cellular level to organ system level.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Sponges (phylum Porifera) possess cells arranged as loose cell aggregates without true tissue formation, exhibiting a cellular level of organisation. In contrast, coelenterates exhibit a tissue level, platyhelminthes exhibit an organ level, and annelids show an organ system level.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The cellular level of organisation with loose cell aggregates is characteristic of sponges.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q02 - Transition from tissue to organ level

questiontext.text: The organ level of body organisation is first observed in members of which animal phylum?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different phyla mark major evolutionary transitions in body complexity. While coelenterates and ctenophores have cells grouped into tissues, higher phyla group tissues into functional organs.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Members of Platyhelminthes are the first to exhibit the organ level of organisation, where distinct tissues assemble into specialized organs. Coelenterates and ctenophores remain at the tissue level, whereas aschelminthes and higher phyla possess organ systems.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The organ level of organisation is characteristic of members of Platyhelminthes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q03 - Definition of incomplete digestive system

questiontext.text: A digestive system is described as incomplete when it:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Digestive systems in animals are classified as complete or incomplete based on the number of openings communicating with the outside.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
An incomplete digestive system has only a single opening to the exterior of the body that functions as both mouth for ingestion and anus for egestion, as seen in Platyhelminthes. In contrast, a complete digestive system has two distinct openings, a mouth and an anus.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
An incomplete digestive system possesses a single external opening that serves as both mouth and anus.

answer.text: Possesses two separate openings at opposite ends
Has a single opening serving as both mouth and anus
Relies exclusively on intracellular digestion within cells

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q04 - Characteristics of open circulatory system

questiontext.text: In an open type of circulatory system, which physiological arrangement is observed?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Circulatory systems are categorised into open and closed types according to the confinement of circulating fluid.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
In an open circulatory system, blood is pumped by the heart into large spaces or sinuses, allowing cells and tissues to be directly bathed in it. In a closed circulatory system, blood circulates continuously through a closed series of vessels of varying diameters including arteries, veins, and capillaries.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
In an open type of circulation, blood is pumped out of the heart and directly bathes the cells and tissues.

answer.text: Blood is confined strictly to a continuous network of vessels
Capillaries mediate all gas exchange without direct tissue contact
Heart is absent and interstitial fluid circulates by ciliary action
Blood is pumped out of the heart directly bathing cells and tissues

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q05 - Planes of division in radial symmetry

questiontext.text: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, the body plan is known as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Body symmetry describes how body parts are arranged relative to a main central axis or plane.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Radial symmetry refers to the condition where any longitudinal plane passing through the central axis divides the organism into two equal, identical halves, as observed in coelenterates, ctenophores, and adult echinoderms. Bilateral symmetry permits division into identical left and right halves in only one plane.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The described body plan is radial symmetry.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q06 - Animal groups exhibiting bilateral body symmetry

questiontext.text: Which pair of animal groups exhibits bilateral symmetry where the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bilateral symmetry is characterised by having a single sagittal plane that divides the animal into mirror-image left and right halves.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Annelids and arthropods possess bilateral symmetry. In contrast, coelenterates, ctenophores, and adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry, while most sponges are asymmetrical.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The pair exhibiting bilateral symmetry consists of annelids and arthropods.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q07 - Germ layers present in diploblastic animals

questiontext.text: In diploblastic animals, which two embryonic germ layers are present, along with an undifferentiated intermediate layer?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Embryonic germ layers give rise to all tissues and organs in multicellular animals during embryonic development.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Diploblastic animals, such as coelenterates, have cells arranged in two primary embryonic germ layers: an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm. Between these two cellular layers lies an undifferentiated, non-cellular layer called mesoglea. Animals with three cellular germ layers including mesoderm are triploblastic.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Diploblastic animals possess external ectoderm and internal endoderm, separated by an undifferentiated layer named mesoglea.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q08 - Taxonomic distribution of triploblastic condition

questiontext.text: Triploblastic organisation, characterised by the presence of a third embryonic layer called mesoderm, is found in which range of phyla?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The evolution of a true cellular mesoderm distinguishes triploblastic animals from diploblastic animals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Sponges lack defined germ layer tissues, and coelenterates and ctenophores are diploblastic. The third germinal layer, mesoderm, between the ectoderm and endoderm, first appears in Platyhelminthes and is retained in all subsequent higher phyla up to Chordata.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Triploblastic organisation is found in animals from Platyhelminthes to Chordata.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q09 - Structural features defining a pseudocoelom

questiontext.text: How is the body cavity structurally arranged in a pseudocoelomate animal such as a roundworm?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A true coelom is defined as a fluid-filled body cavity lined on all sides by mesoderm.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
In pseudocoelomates such as Aschelminthes (roundworms), the body cavity between the gut wall and body wall is not completely lined by mesoderm. Instead, the mesoderm exists as scattered pouches positioned between the ectoderm and endoderm.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
In pseudocoelomates, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm.

answer.text: Present with mesoderm scattered as pouches between ectoderm and endoderm
Completely lined on all sides by mesodermal epithelium
Completely absent, filled solidly with mesodermal parenchyma
Formed by splitting of endoderm within the gut cavity

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q10 - Phylum lacking a body cavity

questiontext.text: Which of the following phyla represents triploblastic animals that completely lack a body cavity (acoelomates)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acoelomates are animals in which no coelom or secondary body cavity exists between the body wall and the gut wall.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical animals that lack a body cavity, making them true acoelomates. Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates, while Annelida and Arthropoda are true coelomates.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Platyhelminthes represents the acoelomate group among triploblastic phyla.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q11 - Distinction among coelomate and pseudocoelomate phyla

questiontext.text: Consider the following animal phyla: Annelida, Aschelminthes, Mollusca, Platyhelminthes, and Echinodermata. How many of these phyla possess a true coelom lined by mesoderm?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Coelomates possess a body cavity completely lined by mesoderm.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Platyhelminthes is acoelomate (no body cavity). Aschelminthes is pseudocoelomate (mesoderm in scattered pouches). Annelida, Mollusca, and Echinodermata are true coelomates possessing a mesodermally lined cavity. Counting the true coelomates gives Annelida, Mollusca, and Echinodermata, making a total of three phyla.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Exactly three of the listed phyla (Annelida, Mollusca, and Echinodermata) are true coelomates.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q12 - Metameric segmentation observed in an earthworm

questiontext.text: The phenomenon where the body is externally and internally divided into segments with serial repetition of at least some organs is called:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
True segmentation involves coordinated divisions across both external and internal body planes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Metamerism (or metameric segmentation) is the structural pattern in which the body is divided into a linear series of similar segments (metameres) both externally and internally, with serial repetition of at least some organs, as typically seen in earthworms (Annelida). Metagenesis refers to alternation of generations, and metamorphosis refers to developmental transformation.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The phenomenon of serial repetition of body segments is known as metamerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q13 - Embryonic origin and position of notochord

questiontext.text: Notochord is an embryonic supporting structure that is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The notochord is a primary diagnostic character defining members of the phylum Chordata.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
According to developmental anatomy, the notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed along the dorsal side of the body during embryonic development in chordates.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The notochord is mesodermally derived and situated on the dorsal side.

answer.text: Mesodermally derived and located on the dorsal side
Ectodermally derived and located on the ventral side
Endodermally derived and located on the lateral side
Mesodermally derived and located on the ventral side

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q14 - Pathway of water transport in sponges

questiontext.text: In sponges, what is the correct sequence of water flow through the canal system?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sponges rely on a water transport or canal system for physiological functions such as food gathering, gas exchange, and waste removal.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Water enters through minute pores called ostia in the body wall, passes into a central cavity named the spongocoel, and exits through a large terminal opening termed the osculum.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The correct pathway of water transport is from ostia into the spongocoel and out through the osculum.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q15 - Role and location of choanocytes in sponges

questiontext.text: Choanocytes, or collar cells, are characteristic cells of sponges that line the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Choanocytes are flagellated collar cells unique to the phylum Porifera.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Choanocytes line the spongocoel and the internal water-conducting canals. Their flagellar beating generates water currents and facilitates intracellular digestion by trapping microscopic food particles.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Choanocytes line the spongocoel and the canals in sponges.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q16 - Reproductive and skeletal features of Porifera

questiontext.text: Which set of biological features correctly describes reproduction and development in sponges?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Poriferans exhibit characteristic reproductive strategies and developmental life cycles adapted to their sessile habit.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Sponges are hermaphrodites (monoecious) because eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual. Fertilisation occurs internally within the parent body, and development is indirect, proceeding through a distinct larval stage that is morphologically different from the adult before settling.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Sponges are hermaphrodite, undergo internal fertilisation, and exhibit indirect development with a morphologically distinct larva.

answer.text: Dioecious, external fertilisation, direct development without a larval stage
Hermaphrodite, external fertilisation, direct development with miniature adults
Dioecious, internal fertilisation, indirect development without free-swimming stage
Hermaphrodite, internal fertilisation, indirect development with morphologically distinct larva

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q17 - Functions of cnidoblasts in cnidarians

questiontext.text: In phylum Cnidaria, cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) containing nematocysts are used for which set of functions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cnidarians derive their name from specialized stinging cells called cnidoblasts or cnidocytes present on their tentacles and body.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Cnidoblasts contain stinging capsules or nematocysts. They serve three primary functions in cnidarians: providing anchorage to the substratum, defending against predators, and capturing prey.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Cnidoblasts function in anchorage, defense, and capture of prey.

answer.text: Water circulation, spicule secretion, and gamete transport

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q18 - Sessile polyp body forms in cnidarians

questiontext.text: In cnidarians, the polyp form is characteristically:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cnidarians exhibit dimorphic body plans represented by polyp and medusa stages.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
The polyp is sessile and cylindrical in shape, exemplified by Hydra and Adamsia. In contrast, the medusa is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming, exemplified by Aurelia (jellyfish).

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The polyp body form is sessile and cylindrical, as seen in Hydra and Adamsia.

answer.text: Sessile and cylindrical, like Hydra and Adamsia

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q19 - Alternation of generations in Obelia

questiontext.text: Which statement accurately describes alternation of generations (metagenesis) in the cnidarian Obelia?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Metagenesis in cnidarians refers to the alternation between asexual sessile polyp forms and sexual free-swimming medusa forms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
In Obelia, the sessile polyp generation produces free-swimming medusae asexually through budding. These medusae release gametes that undergo sexual reproduction and fertilisation, subsequently giving rise to new polyps.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Polyps produce medusae asexually, and medusae form polyps sexually.

answer.text: Polyps produce medusae sexually, and medusae produce polyps asexually
Both polyps and medusae reproduce only by asexual budding
Polyps produce medusae asexually, and medusae form polyps sexually
Polyps develop directly into medusae without producing gametes or buds

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q20 - Comb plates for locomotion in ctenophores

questiontext.text: Ctenophores possess external rows of ciliated comb plates used for locomotion. How many such rows are present on their body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Ctenophora is distinguished by unique locomotor structures known as ciliated comb plates.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
The body of a ctenophore bears eight external longitudinal rows of fused cilia called comb plates, which beat synchronously to propel the organism through marine waters.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Ctenophores possess eight external rows of ciliated comb plates.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q21 - Exclusively marine habitat and bioluminescence in Ctenophora

questiontext.text: Which pair of features uniquely and prominently characterises the phylum Ctenophora?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ctenophores (comb jellies or sea walnuts) possess distinct biological properties that separate them from cnidarians.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
All known ctenophores are exclusively marine, lack cnidoblasts, reproduce solely by sexual means with external fertilisation, and exhibit well-marked bioluminescence (the ability of a living organism to emit light).

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Ctenophores are exclusively marine and exhibit prominent bioluminescence.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q22 - Excretory and osmoregulatory cells in flatworms

questiontext.text: Specialised cells called flame cells found in Platyhelminthes primarily help in:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Flatworms possess specialized excretory structures adapted to regulate fluid balance and eliminate metabolic wastes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Flame cells (solenocytes/protonephridia) are specialised ciliated cells in Platyhelminthes that maintain ionic balance and water volume (osmoregulation) and eliminate metabolic nitrogenous wastes (excretion).

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Flame cells function in osmoregulation and excretion.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q23 - Nutrient absorption and attachment in parasitic flatworms

questiontext.text: Parasitic flatworms like tapeworms show which specific adaptation for maintaining attachment and obtaining nutrition from the host?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Endoparasitic animals evolve specialized morphological and physiological modifications to survive within host bodies.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Parasitic platyhelminths such as Taenia possess hooks and suckers on their scolex for firm anchorage to the host intestinal mucosa. Furthermore, some lack an alimentary canal completely and absorb digested nutrients directly across their permeable body surface.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Parasitic flatworms possess hooks and suckers for attachment and absorb nutrients directly through their body surface.

answer.text: Radula for scraping host tissues and parapodia for attachment
A complete alimentary canal with muscular pharynx for grinding host food
Hooks and suckers for attachment and direct absorption of nutrients through the body surface
Malpighian tubules and tracheal tubes for filter feeding

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q24 - Regeneration capacity and development in flatworms

questiontext.text: Which of the following flatworms is renowned for possessing a high regeneration capacity, and what type of development is characteristic of parasitic platyhelminths?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Platyhelminthes includes both free-living forms with notable regenerative properties and endoparasites with complex multi-stage life cycles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Planaria is a free-living flatworm renowned for its remarkably high capacity for physiological regeneration. In contrast, parasitic members of the phylum (such as liver flukes and tapeworms) exhibit internal fertilisation with development occurring through many larval stages.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Planaria possesses high regeneration capacity, and platyhelminths typically develop through many larval stages.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q25 - Complete alimentary canal with muscular pharynx in roundworms

questiontext.text: The alimentary canal of roundworms (Aschelminthes) is complete and characteristically features a well-developed:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Aschelminthes represents the first phylum in which a complete digestive tract with mouth and anus is established.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
In Aschelminthes (roundworms), the alimentary canal is complete with two openings and features a prominent, highly muscular pharynx that sucks in food material.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The alimentary canal of Aschelminthes has a well-developed muscular pharynx.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q26 - Morphological differences between male and female roundworms

questiontext.text: In the roundworm Ascaris, sexes are separate (dioecious). How can the female be morphologically distinguished from the male?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sexual dimorphism refers to distinct morphological differences between male and female individuals of the same species.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
In Ascaris, the sexes are separate (dioecious). Females are distinctly longer than males and have a straight posterior tip, whereas males are shorter with a characteristic curved posterior end bearing penial spicules.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Female roundworms are typically longer than males.

answer.text: Female is shorter than the male and has a curved posterior end
Female is often longer than the male with a straight posterior end
Female possesses parapodia and suckers while the male lacks them
Female has a dorso-ventrally flattened body while the male is cylindrical

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q27 - Lateral appendages for swimming in Nereis

questiontext.text: Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral unjointed appendages called parapodia, which primarily function in:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Annelids possess specialized muscular and appendage modifications for motility in different environments.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Aquatic annelids such as Nereis bear paired lateral paddle-like extensions of the body wall called parapodia, which function primarily in swimming as well as gas exchange.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Parapodia in Nereis function in swimming.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q28 - Excretory role of nephridia in annelids

questiontext.text: In phylum Annelida, which excretory organs are responsible for osmoregulation and waste removal?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Tubular excretory organs in metameric animals filter coelomic fluid and blood to eliminate nitrogenous waste.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Annelids possess segmentally arranged coiled tubular structures termed nephridia (singular: nephridium). These organs selectively reabsorb useful substances and eliminate waste, thus performing both excretion and osmoregulation. Flame cells occur in flatworms, Malpighian tubules in arthropods, and proboscis glands in hemichordates.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Nephridia serve as osmoregulatory and excretory organs in Annelida.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q29 - Comparison of sexual states in Nereis and earthworm

questiontext.text: Regarding reproduction in Annelida, which statement correctly compares the sexual condition of Nereis with that of earthworms and leeches?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Within the phylum Annelida, different taxa exhibit either separate sexes (dioecy) or combined sexes (monoecy).

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Nereis is an aquatic annelid in which sexes are separate (dioecious). In contrast, earthworms (Pheretima) and blood-sucking leeches (Hirudinaria) possess both male and female reproductive organs in the same individual, making them monoecious (hermaphrodites).

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Nereis is dioecious, whereas earthworms and leeches are monoecious.

answer.text: Nereis is dioecious, whereas earthworms and leeches are monoecious
Nereis is monoecious, whereas earthworms and leeches are dioecious
Both Nereis and earthworms are dioecious, whereas leeches are parthenogenetic
All annelids are strictly monoecious and reproduce exclusively asexually

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q30 - Proportion of named species in Arthropoda

questiontext.text: Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum of Animalia. What proportion of all named animal species on earth belongs to this phylum?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Arthropoda represents the most taxonomically diverse and species-rich phylum on earth.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Over two-thirds of all named animal species described on earth belong to the phylum Arthropoda, primarily driven by the immense diversity of class Insecta.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Over two-thirds of all named species on earth are arthropods.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q31 - Diverse respiratory organs in arthropods

questiontext.text: Which combination of respiratory organs is found across various terrestrial and aquatic members of phylum Arthropoda?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Arthropods occupy marine, freshwater, and terrestrial habitats, leading to diverse respiratory adaptations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Aquatic forms (such as prawns and king crabs) respire via gills or book gills. Terrestrial arachnids (such as scorpions and spiders) possess book lungs, while insects utilize a network of tubes called a tracheal system.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Arthropods respire via gills, book gills, book lungs, or a tracheal system.

answer.text: Gills, book gills, book lungs, or tracheal system

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q32 - Classification of arthropods by ecological and medical role

questiontext.text: Match the arthropods correctly to their categorisation: Locusta is a gregarious pest, Limulus is a living fossil, and Apis is an economically important insect. Which of the following sets correctly classifies these animals?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Arthropods exhibit wide ecological roles categorized into economically important insects, disease vectors, pests, and ancient relict lineages.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Apis (honey bee) produces honey and wax (economically important). Locusta (locust) swarms in large numbers destroying vegetation (gregarious pest). Limulus (king crab) has survived for millions of years with minimal morphological change (living fossil).

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Locusta is a gregarious pest, Limulus is a living fossil, and Apis is an economically important insect.

answer.text: Locusta: living fossil; Limulus: vector; Apis: pest
Locusta: vector; Limulus: gregarious pest; Apis: living fossil
Locusta: economically important insect; Limulus: vector; Apis: living fossil
Locusta: gregarious pest; Limulus: living fossil; Apis: economically important insect

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q33 - Three primary body regions in molluscs

questiontext.text: The unsegmented soft body of a typical mollusc is divided into which three distinct regions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Molluscs, the second largest animal phylum, have a soft, unsegmented body plan.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
The molluscan body consists of three primary regions: an anterior sensory head, a ventral muscular foot used for locomotion, and a dorsal visceral hump containing internal organ systems.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The molluscan body is divided into head, muscular foot, and visceral hump.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q34 - Feeding organ radula in molluscs

questiontext.text: What is the structure and function of the radula found in the mouth of molluscs?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Molluscs possess specialized feeding apparatus adapted for scraping or grinding food particles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
The mouth of many molluscs contains a unique file-like rasping organ called the radula, which bears transverse rows of minute chitinous teeth used to scrape food from surfaces.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The radula is a file-like rasping organ used for feeding.

answer.text: Calcareous shell for protecting the visceral hump
Feather-like gill for gas exchange in mantle cavity

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q35 - Functions of feather-like gills in mantle cavity

questiontext.text: In molluscs, a soft and spongy layer of skin forms a mantle over the visceral hump. What is the space between the hump and the mantle called, and what dual functions do the feather-like gills within it perform?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The mantle cavity is a key anatomical feature of phylum Mollusca housing specialized respiratory structures.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
The space enclosed between the visceral hump and the mantle fold is the mantle cavity. Located inside this cavity are feather-like ctenidia (gills) that serve dual physiological functions: respiration (gas exchange) and excretion (removal of wastes).

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The space is the mantle cavity, and the gills carry out respiratory and excretory functions.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q36 - Developmental shift in symmetry in echinoderms

questiontext.text: Echinoderms display a distinctive shift in body symmetry during their life cycle. Which pattern of symmetry is exhibited by adult and larval echinoderms, respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Echinoderms undergo a metamorphosis that alters their primary body axes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Adult echinoderms possess pentamerous radial symmetry, while their free-swimming ciliated larvae possess bilateral symmetry. This demonstrates that their radial symmetry is secondary and derived from a bilateral ancestor.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical, whereas their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

answer.text: Adults are bilaterally symmetrical, while larvae are radially symmetrical
Both adults and larvae are strictly asymmetrical
Both adults and larvae are radially symmetrical
Adults are radially symmetrical, while larvae are bilaterally symmetrical

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q37 - Functions of water vascular system in echinoderms

questiontext.text: The most distinctive feature of echinoderms is the presence of a water vascular system. Which set of functions does this system perform?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The water vascular system (ambulacral system) is a hydraulic network of canals unique to echinoderms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
The water vascular system operates hydraulic tube feet (podia) that aid in locomotion, assist in capturing and transporting food to the mouth, and facilitate respiratory gas exchange across thin epithelial membranes.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The water vascular system aids in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration.

answer.text: Locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q38 - Digestive orientation and excretion in echinoderms

questiontext.text: Regarding the digestive and excretory systems of echinoderms, which statement is completely correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Echinoderms possess a complete digestive tract arranged along their oral-aboral axis, but lack specialized excretory organs.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
In echinoderms, the complete alimentary canal has the mouth located on the lower or ventral (oral) surface and the anus situated on the upper or dorsal (aboral) surface. Nitrogenous excretion occurs primarily via simple diffusion through tube feet and respiratory surfaces because a specialized excretory system is entirely absent.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The mouth is on the lower (ventral) side, the anus is on the upper (dorsal) side, and a specialized excretory system is absent.

answer.text: Mouth is on the dorsal side, anus on the ventral side, and Malpighian tubules perform excretion
Mouth is on the lower (ventral) side, anus on the upper (dorsal) side, and an excretory system is absent
Digestive system is incomplete with a single opening, and nephridia perform excretion
Mouth is terminal, anus is absent, and flame cells perform osmoregulation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q39 - Three anatomical regions of cylindrical hemichordate body

questiontext.text: The cylindrical body of a hemichordate (such as Balanoglossus) is composed of which three anatomical divisions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hemichordates are marine worm-like organisms characterized by a tripartite body construction.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
The cylindrical body of a hemichordate consists of an anterior pre-oral proboscis, a middle muscular collar, and an elongated posterior trunk.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The body is composed of an anterior proboscis, collar, and long trunk.

answer.text: Anterior proboscis, collar, and a long trunk

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q40 - Circulatory, excretory, and skeletal features of Hemichordata

questiontext.text: Which combination correctly describes the circulatory system, excretory organ, and rudimentary notochord-like structure in Hemichordata?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hemichordata was previously considered a subphylum of Chordata due to a collar structure once thought to be a notochord, but is now recognized as a distinct non-chordate phylum.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Hemichordates possess an open circulatory system, carry out excretion using a proboscis gland situated in the pre-oral region, and have a rudimentary diverticulum termed a stomochord located in the collar region.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Hemichordates have an open circulatory system, an excretory proboscis gland, and a stomochord in the collar.

answer.text: Closed circulatory system; flame cells; notochord in the tail region
Open circulatory system; Malpighian tubules; dorsal nerve cord only
Open circulatory system; proboscis gland; stomochord in the collar region

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q41 - Diagnostic morphological hallmarks of Chordata

questiontext.text: Animals belonging to phylum Chordata are fundamentally characterized by which set of structural features?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
All chordates share four primary anatomical hallmarks at some point during their embryonic or adult life.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
The diagnostic features of Chordata are: a longitudinal supporting notochord, a single dorsal hollow nerve cord, paired pharyngeal gill slits, and a post-anal tail, along with a ventral muscular heart.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Chordates are characterized by a notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, and paired pharyngeal gill slits.

answer.text: Notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, and paired pharyngeal gill slits
Ventral solid nerve cord, dorsal heart, and absent notochord
Chitinous exoskeleton, open circulation, and tracheal system
Calcareous shell, ventral visceral hump, and mantle cavity

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q42 - Extent and persistence of notochord in protochordates

questiontext.text: How does the distribution and persistence of the notochord differ between subphylum Urochordata and subphylum Cephalochordata?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protochordates (Urochordata and Cephalochordata) are distinguished based on the anatomical distribution and life-stage retention of the notochord.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
In Urochordata (tunicates like Ascidia), the notochord is present only in the tail of the free-swimming larva and is lost during metamorphosis. In Cephalochordata (lancelets like Branchiostoma), the notochord extends from the tip of the rostrum to the tail and persists throughout the entire life of the organism.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The notochord is restricted to the larval tail in Urochordata, whereas in Cephalochordata it extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.

answer.text: In Urochordata it extends from head to tail throughout life; in Cephalochordata it is restricted to the larval tail
In Urochordata it is present only in the larval tail; in Cephalochordata it extends from head to tail and persists throughout life
In both subphyla it is replaced by a bony vertebral column in adults
In Urochordata it is absent entirely; in Cephalochordata it forms only during the adult reproductive phase

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q43 - Mouth and respiratory gill slits in Cyclostomata

questiontext.text: Members of the jawless vertebrate class Cyclostomata possess which pair of morphological characteristics?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Class Cyclostomata comprises primitive, jawless, eel-like vertebrates belonging to the division Agnatha.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Cyclostomes have an elongated body bearing a circular, sucking mouth devoid of jaws, and 6 to 15 pairs of lateral gill slits for aquatic respiration. They also lack scales and paired fins.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Cyclostomes possess a circular sucking mouth without jaws and 6 to 15 pairs of gill slits.

answer.text: Jaws with placoid teeth and 4 pairs of operculated gill slits
Terminal mouth with operculum, and cycloid scales
Sucking and circular mouth without jaws, and 6 to 15 pairs of gill slits
Beak without teeth, and pneumatic hollow bones

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q44 - Absence of air bladder in cartilaginous fishes

questiontext.text: Cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes) must swim constantly in water to avoid sinking because they lack a:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Buoyancy regulation in fishes is typically mediated by a specialized gas-filled organ known as the swim bladder or air bladder.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Members of class Chondrichthyes (such as sharks and rays) lack an air bladder (swim bladder). Consequently, they are negatively buoyant and must swim continuously to generate hydrodynamic lift and avoid sinking to the bottom.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Cartilaginous fishes must swim constantly because they lack an air bladder.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q45 - Comparison between cartilaginous and bony fishes

questiontext.text: Which row of contrasting characters correctly distinguishes Chondrichthyes from Osteichthyes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fishes are divided into cartilaginous (Chondrichthyes) and bony (Osteichthyes) classes based on skeletal, scale, and gill morphology.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Chondrichthyes possess a ventral mouth, skin covered with minute placoid scales, separate gill slits lacking an operculum, and a cartilaginous skeleton. Osteichthyes possess a terminal mouth, skin covered with cycloid or ctenoid scales, four pairs of gills covered by an operculum, and a bony skeleton.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
Chondrichthyes have a ventral mouth, placoid scales, and naked gill slits, whereas Osteichthyes have a terminal mouth, cycloid or ctenoid scales, and an operculum.

answer.text: Chondrichthyes: ventral mouth, placoid scales, gill slits without operculum; Osteichthyes: terminal mouth, cycloid/ctenoid scales, operculum present
Chondrichthyes: terminal mouth, cycloid scales, operculum present; Osteichthyes: ventral mouth, placoid scales, operculum absent
Chondrichthyes: bony endoskeleton, viviparous, air bladder present; Osteichthyes: cartilaginous endoskeleton, oviparous, air bladder absent
Chondrichthyes: four-chambered heart, warm-blooded; Osteichthyes: two-chambered heart, cold-blooded

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q46 - Cloaca and three-chambered heart in Amphibia

questiontext.text: In amphibians, the alimentary canal, urinary, and reproductive tracts open into a common exit chamber called the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In many non-mammalian tetrapods, multiple physiological systems terminate in a single distal chamber.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
In amphibians, the terminal ends of the digestive tract, urinary ducts, and genital ducts converge into a shared chamber termed the cloaca, which opens directly to the exterior.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The common exit chamber in amphibians is the cloaca.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q47 - Heart chamber configuration across reptile groups

questiontext.text: The heart in class Reptilia is typically three-chambered with incomplete ventricular division. Which reptile represents an exception by possessing a completely four-chambered heart?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vertebrate cardiac evolution exhibits progressive partitioning of cardiac chambers from fish to mammals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Most reptiles (snakes, lizards, turtles) possess a three-chambered heart consisting of two atria and an incompletely divided ventricle. However, crocodilians (including Crocodilus and Alligator) possess a completely divided ventricle, resulting in a fully four-chambered heart.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The crocodile possesses an exceptional four-chambered heart among reptiles.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q48 - Distinctive characters separating Aves and Mammalia

questiontext.text: Both birds (Aves) and mammals (Mammalia) are homoiothermous with four-chambered hearts. Which unique anatomical feature is exclusive to class Mammalia and absent in Aves?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Although birds and mammals share homeothermy and a four-chambered heart, each class possesses distinct diagnostic integumentary and physiological traits.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
Mammals are uniquely characterized by milk-producing mammary glands for nourishing their young, hair covering the skin, and external ear pinnae. Pneumatic bones are specific to birds, while internal fertilisation, ossified skeletons, and pulmonary respiration are shared by both groups.

Step 3: Conclusion and Final Answer
The presence of mammary glands and skin hair is exclusive to mammals.

answer.text: Mammary glands to nourish young ones and hair on the skin
